title: Nashville Hot Smash Burger
changes_from_base: Same smash method as the Classic. A cayenne hot oil is warmed and brushed over the patties after the flip, and a cool yoghurt-mayo sauce, pickles and lettuce balance the heat.
summary: Smash-burger patties are brushed with a fiery Nashville-style spiced oil straight off the heat, then cooled down with a yoghurt mayo and crunchy pickles.
equipment: large cast-iron or heavy steel frying pan (at least 26 cm) or flat griddle
stiff metal spatula (fish slice or burger turner)

ingredients.item: soft burger buns or brioche-style buns

steps.title: Make the cooling sauce
steps.text: Stir together the mayonnaise, Greek yoghurt, lemon juice and garlic powder, then chill it until needed. The yoghurt's tang and cool creaminess are there to balance the chilli heat coming later, so don't skip chilling it properly.

steps.title: Make the Nashville hot oil
steps.text: Warm the oil in a small pan over low-medium heat for about 1 minute until it looks shimmering-warm but is not smoking - around 120°C is plenty. Take it off the heat before whisking in the cayenne, paprika, garlic powder, brown sugar and salt; adding the spices off the heat stops the cayenne scorching and turning bitter, and the mix should stay a deep brick red rather than dark brown.

steps.title: Toast the buns
steps.text: Butter the cut sides of the buns and toast them cut-side down in a hot pan over medium heat for 1-2 minutes until golden. Set aside; the toasted crumb will hold up against the sauces without turning soft.

steps.title: Heat the pan and smash
steps.text: Get the same pan dry and fiercely hot over high heat for 4-5 minutes, until a flicked drop of water skitters and vanishes instantly. Add 2-3 beef balls, spaced well apart, cover with baking paper, and press hard with a spatula for 20-30 seconds until flattened to about 6mm - then leave them alone.

steps.title: Season and sear
steps.text: Peel off the paper and season the tops with salt and pepper. Sear undisturbed for 2-2.5 minutes until the underside is deeply browned and lacy at the edges, the crust that gives the beef its depth of flavour.

steps.title: Flip and melt the cheese
steps.text: Scrape firmly to lift the crust, flip, and lay cheese on half the patties. Cook for 45-60 seconds until the beef shows no pink and reaches 71°C, with the juices running clear.

steps.title: Brush with hot oil off the heat
steps.text: Lift the patties onto a plate away from the hot pan before brushing them generously with the hot oil - doing this on the pan would scorch the cayenne and turn it bitter. Stir the oil well before each brushing, since the spices settle to the bottom quickly, then stack a cheese-topped patty with a plain one.

steps.title: Build the burger
steps.text: Spread the cooling sauce on the bottom bun and add a layer of lettuce. Stack the hot-oiled patties on top, scatter over pickles - the classic partner to Nashville-style heat - then spread more cooling sauce on the top bun before closing the burger.

tips: Keep the oil off direct heat while you whisk in the spices - cayenne scorches fast and turns bitter if it hits a hot pan.
Stir the hot oil again just before each brushing, since the ground spices settle to the bottom between uses.
Brush the oil onto the patties once they're off the pan, not while they're still searing, or it will burn instead of flavouring the meat.
Take care around the cayenne fumes when whisking the hot oil - work in a well-ventilated spot.
storage: Cooked patties keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days, or frozen for up to 2 months; thaw fully before reheating. Warm through in a hot pan until piping hot and the centre reaches 74°C, then brush with a little fresh hot oil rather than storing it brushed on.
